title.zh: 卷一百〇八 列傳第五十八: 韋見素 崔圓 崔渙 杜鴻漸
title.en: Volume 108 Biographies 58: Wei Jiansu, Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, Du Hongjian
title.raw: 卷一百〇八 列傳第五十八: 韋見素 崔圓 崔渙 杜鴻漸 Volume 108 Biographies 58: Wei Jiansu, Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, Du Hongjian

sentences.zh: 杜鴻漸

translations.literal: Du Hongjian
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian

sentences.zh: 韋見素，字會微，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Jiansu, courtesy name Huiwei, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiansu, whose courtesy name was Huiwei, came from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 父湊，開元中太原尹。

translations.literal: His father Cou served as Intendant of Taiyuan in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cou had been intendant of Taiyuan during the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 見素學科登第。

translations.literal: Jiansu passed the specialized examination and received his degree.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu passed the specialized civil-service examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，解褐相王府參軍，歷衛佐、河南府倉曹。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he left commoner status to become a staff officer in the Prince of Xiang's mansion, and successively served as a guard aide and as granary clerk in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period he took his first office as a staff officer in the household of the Prince of Xiang, then served as a guard aide and as granary clerk in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，起為大理寺丞，襲爵彭城郡公。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was recalled as vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review and inherited the title Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed the mourning period, and when it ended he was appointed vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review and succeeded to the dukedom of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 坐事出為坊州司馬。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was sent out to serve as military aide in Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted to military aide in Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為庫部員外郎，加朝散大夫，歷右司兵部二員外，左司兵部二郎中，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as two vice-director posts in the right and left secretariats of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, held two vice-director posts in the war ministry's right and left secretariats in turn, and was then promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 天寶五年，充江西、山南、黔中、嶺南等黜陟使，觀省風俗，彈糾長吏，所至肅然。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Jiangxi, Shannan, Qianzhong, Lingnan, and other circuits, inspecting local customs and impeaching chief officials; wherever he went order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5 he was appointed promotion-and-demotion commissioner for Jiangxi, Shannan, Qianzhong, Lingnan, and other regions, reviewing local customs and impeaching senior officials, and everywhere he went the administration grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜給事中，駁正繩違，頗振臺閣舊典。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission he was appointed Attendant Gentleman, where he corrected errors and restrained violations and greatly revived the old standards of the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Attendant Gentleman, correcting abuses and restraining misconduct and thereby reviving much of the censorate's former practice.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校尚書工部侍郎，改右丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting vice-minister of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and then transferred to right vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting vice-minister of works and then transferred to the post of right vice-director.

sentences.zh: 九載，遷吏部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to vice-minister of personnel and given the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became vice-minister of personnel and was granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 見素仁恕長者，意不忤物，及典選累年，銓敘平允，人士稱之。

translations.literal: Jiansu was a benevolent and forgiving elder whose mind gave no offense to others; when he presided over selections for many years his evaluations were fair and even, and men of standing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu was a kindly, forbearing man who never gave offense; during his many years in charge of appointments his ratings were even-handed, and he was widely respected.

sentences.zh: 時右相楊國忠用事，左相陳希烈畏其權寵，凡事唯諾，無敢發明，玄宗頗知之，聖情不悅。

translations.literal: At that time the right chancellor Yang Guozhong held power; the left chancellor Chen Xilie feared his authority and favor and in all matters merely assented, daring to clarify nothing. Emperor Xuanzong was quite aware of this, and his sacred mind was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The right chancellor Yang Guozhong then dominated the government, while the left chancellor Chen Xilie, fearing Yang's power, merely assented to everything and never spoke his mind. Xuanzong noticed this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三年秋，霖雨六十餘日，京師廬舍垣墉頹毀殆盡，凡一十九坊汙潦。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the thirteenth year of Tianbao rain fell for more than sixty days; in the capital dwellings and walls were nearly all destroyed, and nineteen wards were flooded.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tianbao 13 it rained for more than sixty days. In the capital nearly every house and wall collapsed, and nineteen wards lay under water.

sentences.zh: 天子以宰輔或未稱職，見此咎征，命楊國忠精求端士，時兵部侍郎吉溫方承寵遇，上意用之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought the chief ministers might not be fit for their posts and, seeing this omen of blame, ordered Yang Guozhong to search carefully for upright men. At that time the vice-minister of war Ji Wen was enjoying favor, and the emperor intended to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the disaster as a sign that his chief ministers were unfit and ordered Yang Guozhong to find worthy replacements. Ji Wen, vice-minister of war, was then in favor, and the emperor meant to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 國忠以溫祿山賓佐，懼其威權，奏寢其事。

translations.literal: Guozhong, because Wen had been a retainer of An Lushan, feared his power and authority and memorialized to shelve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong, knowing that Wen had once served An Lushan, feared his influence and persuaded the emperor to drop the appointment.

sentences.zh: 國忠訪於中書舍人竇華、宋昱等，華、昱言見素方雅，柔而易制。

translations.literal: Guozhong consulted the Secretariat drafters Dou Hua, Song Yu, and others; Hua and Yu said Jiansu was upright and refined, gentle and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong asked the Secretariat drafters Dou Hua and Song Yu for advice; they said Jiansu was upright and refined, mild, and easy to manage.

sentences.zh: 上亦以經事相王府，有舊恩，可之。

translations.literal: The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had long served in the Prince of Xiang's household and owed him an old debt of kindness, and approved the choice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also remembered Jiansu's long service in his own household when he was Prince of Xiang and approved the appointment.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，拜武部尚書、同中書門下平章事，充集賢院學士，知門下省事，代陳希烈。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he was appointed Minister of War and Grand Councilor with concurrent duty in the Secretariat and Chancellery, made a scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, given charge of Chancellery affairs, and replaced Chen Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: That August he was made minister of war and grand councilor, appointed a scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, put in charge of chancellery business, and replaced Chen Xilie.

sentences.zh: 見素既為國忠引用，心德之。

translations.literal: Since Jiansu had been brought in by Guozhong, he was grateful to him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Having been advanced by Guozhong, Jiansu felt deep gratitude toward him.

sentences.zh: 時祿山與國忠爭寵，兩相猜嫌，見素亦無所是非，署字而已，遂至凶胡犯順，不措一言。

translations.literal: At that time Lushan and Guozhong were contending for favor and each suspected the other; Jiansu too made no judgment of right or wrong and merely affixed his signature, until the wicked barbarian rose in rebellion and he offered not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan and Guozhong were then rivals for imperial favor and deeply suspicious of each other. Jiansu likewise passed no judgment and merely signed documents, and when the rebel rose he never spoke a word of protest.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月，哥舒翰兵敗桃林，潼關不守。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Geshu Han's army was defeated at Taolin and Tong Pass could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year Geshu Han was defeated at Taolin, and Tong Pass fell.

sentences.zh: 是月，玄宗蒼黃出幸，莫知所詣。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Xuanzong fled in haste on a tour, and no one knew where he was bound.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Xuanzong fled the capital in panic, and no one knew where he intended to go.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠以身領劍南旄鉞，請幸成都。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong, who personally held the military command of Jiannan, requested that the emperor tour Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, who held military command in Jiannan in his own person, urged the emperor to flee to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 見素與國忠、御史大夫魏方進遇上於延秋門，便扈從之咸陽。

translations.literal: Jiansu, together with Guozhong and the Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin, met the emperor at Yanqiu Gate and then escorted him to Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu met the emperor at Yanqiu Gate with Guozhong and Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin and escorted him to Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 翌日，次馬嵬驛，軍士不得食，流言不遜。

translations.literal: The next day they halted at Mawei Post; the soldiers had no food, and insolent rumors spread.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they stopped at Mawei Post. The troops had nothing to eat, and mutinous talk spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 龍武將軍陳玄禮懼其亂，乃與飛龍馬家李護國謀於皇太子，請誅國忠，以慰士心。

translations.literal: The Dragon Martial general Chen Xuanli, fearing disorder, then plotted with Li Huguo of the Flying Dragon stud and the Crown Prince to request the execution of Guozhong in order to calm the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Martial general Chen Xuanli, fearing a mutiny, conspired with Li Huguo of the imperial stud and the crown prince to have Guozhong killed and thereby appease the troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，玄禮等禁軍圍行宮，盡誅楊氏。

translations.literal: That day Xuanli and the other imperial guards surrounded the traveling palace and put the entire Yang clan to death.
translations.idiomatic: That day Chen Xuanli and the imperial guards surrounded the temporary palace and killed every member of the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 見素遁走，為亂兵所傷，眾呼曰：「勿傷韋相！

translations.literal: Jiansu fled and was wounded by the mutinous troops; the crowd cried, "Do not harm Chancellor Wei!
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu fled and was wounded in the melee; the soldiers shouted, "Do not harm Chancellor Wei!

sentences.zh: 」識者救之，獲免。

translations.literal: " Those who knew him rescued him, and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: " Men who recognized him pulled him to safety, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，令壽王瑁宣慰，賜藥傅瘡。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sent Prince Shou Li Mao to offer consolation and gave medicine to dress his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard what had happened, he sent Prince Shou Li Mao to comfort him and provided medicine for his wounds.

sentences.zh: 魏方進為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Wei Fangjin was killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fangjin was killed by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 是日，朝士獨見素一人。

translations.literal: That day Jiansu alone remained among the court officials.
translations.idiomatic: That day Jiansu was the only court official still with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是夜宿馬嵬，上命見素子京兆府司錄參軍諤為御史中丞，充置頓使。

translations.literal: That night they lodged at Mawei; the emperor appointed Jiansu's son E, a recording officer in the Jingzhao prefectural staff, vice censor-in-chief and made him provisioning commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They spent the night at Mawei. The emperor appointed Jiansu's son E, a staff officer in the Jingzhao prefecture, vice censor-in-chief and commissioner for arranging the imperial halt.

sentences.zh: 淩晨將發，六軍將士曰：「國忠反叛，不可更往蜀川，請之河、隴。

translations.literal: Just before dawn, as they were about to depart, the officers and soldiers of the Six Armies said, "Guozhong rebelled; we must not go on to Shu. We ask to go to the Yellow River region and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, just before departure, the officers and men of the Six Armies declared, "Guozhong was a traitor; we cannot go on to Shu. Take us to the northwest instead.

sentences.zh: 」或言靈武、太原，或云還京，議者不一。

translations.literal: " Some spoke of Lingwu or Taiyuan, others of returning to the capital, and opinions were divided.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Lingwu or Taiyuan, others a return to the capital, and no agreement could be reached.

sentences.zh: 上意在劍南，慮違士心，無所言。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was set on Jiannan, but fearing to go against the soldiers' wishes he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still meant to go to Jiannan but, fearing to defy the troops, said nothing.

sentences.zh: 諤曰：「還京須有捍賊之備。

translations.literal: E said, "To return to the capital we must have preparations to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: E said, "If we return to the capital we must have the means to hold off the rebels.

sentences.zh: 今兵馬數少，恐非萬全，不如且至扶風，徐圖去就。

translations.literal: Our troops are now few in number and the plan may not be fully secure; it would be better first to go to Fufeng and slowly consider where to go next.
translations.idiomatic: We have too few troops for that to be safe. Better go first to Fufeng and decide our next move from there.

sentences.zh: 」上詢於眾，眾以為然，乃令皇太子後殿。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked the assembly, and all agreed; he then ordered the Crown Prince to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor put the question to those present, all agreed, and he ordered the crown prince to guard the rear.

sentences.zh: 上至扶風郡，從駕諸軍各圖去就，頗出醜言。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Fufeng Prefecture, the various armies accompanying him each plotted their own course and uttered many ugly words.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Fufeng Prefecture, the troops in his train each began planning to go their own way, and discontent spread openly.

sentences.zh: 陳玄禮不能制，上聞之憂懼。

translations.literal: Chen Xuanli could not control them; when the emperor heard of it he was anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuanli could not restrain them, and the emperor grew deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 會益州貢春彩十萬疋，乃以其綱使濛陽尉劉景溫為監察御史，其彩悉陳於廷，召六軍將士等入，上謂之曰：「卿等皆國之功臣，勛勞素著，朕之優賞，常亦不輕。

translations.literal: It happened that Yi Prefecture had presented one hundred thousand bolts of spring brocade as tribute; he made the convoy leader, Mengyang district magistrate Liu Jingwen, an investigating censor, had all the brocade displayed in the courtyard, summoned the officers and soldiers of the Six Armies, and said to them, "You are all meritorious servants of the state, your achievements long renowned; my generous rewards to you have never been slight.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a tribute convoy from Yi Prefecture arrived with one hundred thousand bolts of spring brocade. The emperor made the convoy leader, Mengyang magistrate Liu Jingwen, an investigating censor, had all the cloth laid out in the courtyard, and summoned the officers and men of the Six Armies. He told them, "You are all meritorious servants of the state, and I have never been stingy in rewarding you.

sentences.zh: 逆胡負恩，事須回避，甚知卿等不得別父母妻子，朕亦不及辭九廟。

translations.literal: The rebellious barbarian has betrayed his grace; we must withdraw. I know well that you could not take leave of your parents, wives, and children, and I too had no time to bid farewell at the ancestral shrines.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel has forced us to flee. I know you could not say farewell to your parents, wives, and children, and I myself had no time even to take leave at the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 」言發涕流。

translations.literal: " As he spoke tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: " As he spoke, he wept openly.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕今須幸蜀，蜀路險狹，人若多往，恐難祗供。

translations.literal: He went on, "I must now tour Shu. The road to Shu is narrow and perilous; if too many go, I fear supplies cannot be provided.
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "I must now go to Shu. The road is narrow and difficult, and if too many follow me there will not be enough to sustain you all.

sentences.zh: 今有此彩，卿等即宜分取，各自圖去就。

translations.literal: Now that this brocade is here, you should at once divide it among yourselves and each decide where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Take this brocade and divide it among yourselves, and each of you may go wherever you choose.

sentences.zh: 朕自有子弟、中官等相隨，便與卿等訣別。

translations.literal: I have my own sons, younger kinsmen, and palace eunuchs to accompany me, and will now take leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: My sons, younger kinsmen, and eunuchs will accompany me, and I must now bid you farewell.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸俯伏號泣，曰：「死生從陛下。

translations.literal: " All prostrated themselves, weeping aloud, and said, "In life or death we follow Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: " They all prostrated themselves, weeping, and cried, "In life or in death we follow Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上良久曰：「去住聽卿自便。

translations.literal: " After a long silence the emperor said, "Whether you stay or go is for you to decide as you please.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long pause the emperor said, "Whether you stay or go is entirely for you to decide.

sentences.zh: 」自是醜言方息。

translations.literal: " From then on the ugly talk finally ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did the mutinous talk subside.

sentences.zh: 七月，至巴西郡，以見素兼左相、武部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they reached Baxi Prefecture, and Jiansu was given concurrent posts as left chancellor and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they reached Baxi Prefecture, and Jiansu was made left chancellor while retaining the ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 數日，至蜀郡，加金紫光祿大夫，進封豳國公，與一子五品官。

translations.literal: A few days later they reached Shu Prefecture; he was given the title Grand Master of Glorious Splendor with Golden Seal, advanced to Duke of Bin, and one son was granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later they reached Shu Prefecture. He was granted the title Grand Master of Glorious Splendor with Golden Seal, created Duke of Bin, and one of his sons was given a fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 是月，皇太子即位於靈武，道路艱澀，音驛未通。

translations.literal: That month the Crown Prince took the throne at Lingwu; the roads were difficult and courier posts had not yet been restored.
translations.idiomatic: That month the crown prince ascended the throne at Lingwu, but the roads were treacherous and no reliable word reached the fugitive court.

sentences.zh: 八月，肅宗使至，始知靈武即位。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an envoy from Emperor Suzong arrived, and only then did they learn of the enthronement at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an envoy from Suzong arrived, and only then did they learn that he had already taken the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 尋命見素與宰臣房琯賫傳國寶玉冊奉使靈武，宣傳詔命，便行冊禮。

translations.literal: Soon Jiansu and the chief minister Fang Guan were ordered to carry the imperial seal and jade registers on a mission to Lingwu to proclaim the edicts and perform the investiture rites at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiansu and chief minister Fang Guan were sent to Lingwu bearing the imperial seal and jade registers to proclaim the succession and perform the investiture ceremony.

sentences.zh: 將行，上皇謂見素等曰：「皇帝自幼仁孝，與諸子有異，朕豈不知。

translations.literal: As they were about to depart, the Retired Emperor said to Jiansu and the others, "The Emperor has been benevolent and filial from childhood and unlike my other sons; how could I not know this?
translations.idiomatic: Before they set out, the retired emperor told Jiansu and the others, "The emperor has been filial and humane since childhood, unlike my other sons, and I have always known it.

sentences.zh: 往十三年，已有傳位之意，屬其歲水旱，左右勸朕且俟豐年。

translations.literal: Thirteen years ago I already intended to pass the throne, but that year brought flood and drought, and those around me urged me to wait for a year of abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years ago I already meant to abdicate, but floods and drought struck that year, and my advisers urged me to wait for a better harvest.

sentences.zh: 爾來便屬祿山構逆，方隅震擾，未遂此心。

translations.literal: Since then it fell to Lushan to plot rebellion and the regions to be shaken in turmoil, and this wish was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Then An Lushan rebelled and the empire was thrown into chaos, and I never carried out that plan.

sentences.zh: 昨發馬嵬，亦有處分。

translations.literal: When we set out from Mawei yesterday there were also arrangements made.
translations.idiomatic: Even when we left Mawei I had already made arrangements for the succession.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝受命，朕心頓如釋負。

translations.literal: Now that the Emperor has received the mandate, my heart is suddenly as if a burden had been lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the emperor has taken the throne, a great weight has lifted from my heart.

sentences.zh: 勞卿等遠去，勉輔佐之。

translations.literal: I trouble you to go so far; strive to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: I am sorry to send you so far, but do your utmost to assist him.

sentences.zh: 多難興王，自古皆有，卿等乃心王室，以宗社為念，早定中原，吾之望也。

translations.literal: Kings have risen through hardship since antiquity; devote your hearts to the royal house, keep the altars of state in mind, and restore the central plains soon — that is my hope.
translations.idiomatic: Kings have often risen through hardship; devote yourselves to the dynasty, think of the altars of state, and recover the central plains as soon as you can. That is my hope.

sentences.zh: 」見素等悲泣不自勝。

translations.literal: " Jiansu and the others wept in grief beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiansu and the others wept until they could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 仍以見素子諤及中書舍人賈至充冊禮使判官。

translations.literal: Jiansu's son E and the Secretariat drafter Jia Zhi were also made adjutants to the investiture mission.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu's son E and Secretariat drafter Jia Zhi were appointed adjutants to the investiture mission.

sentences.zh: 時肅宗已回幸順化郡。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Suzong had already returned to tour Shunhua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By then Suzong had already moved his court to Shunhua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，見素等至，冊禮畢，從幸彭原郡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jiansu and the others arrived; when the investiture rites were completed they accompanied the emperor on his tour to Pengyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jiansu and his party arrived, completed the investiture, and accompanied Suzong to Pengyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在東宮，素聞房琯名重，故虛懷以待；

translations.literal: When Suzong was in the Eastern Palace he had long heard that Fang Guan's reputation was weighty and therefore received him with open humility;
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong had been crown prince he had long heard of Fang Guan's reputation and received him with respect;

sentences.zh: 以見素常附國忠，禮遇稍薄。

translations.literal: because Jiansu had long attached himself to Guozhong, his treatment was somewhat less generous.
translations.idiomatic: but because Jiansu had long been allied with Guozhong, his treatment was somewhat cooler.

sentences.zh: 明年，至鳳翔。

translations.literal: The following year they reached Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court reached Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 三月，除左僕射，罷知政事，以憲部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the third month he was removed from the post of left vice-director, ceased serving in state affairs, and retired with the title Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was relieved of the left vice-directorship and of his duties in government, retiring with the title minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿代為左相。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing replaced him as left chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing replaced him as left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗在鳳翔，喪亂之後，綱紀未立，兵吏三銓，簿籍煨燼，南曹選人，文符悉多偽濫。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Suzong was at Fengxiang, after the calamity of rebellion discipline had not yet been established; the three boards for military and civil selection had their registers burned to ashes, and among candidates at the southern bureau documents were largely forged and spurious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Suzong's court was at Fengxiang after the rebellion, government discipline had collapsed. The personnel registers of the three selection boards had been burned, and candidates at the southern bureau submitted largely forged credentials.

sentences.zh: 上以凶醜未滅，且示招懷，據到註擬，一無檢括。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the wicked enemy had not yet been destroyed and wishing to show conciliation, approved appointments on the basis of whatever documents arrived, with no examination at all.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebels had not yet been crushed and the emperor wished to win support, he approved appointments on whatever papers were submitted, without any review.

sentences.zh: 見素曰：「臣典選歲久，周知此弊。

translations.literal: Jiansu said, "Your servant has presided over selections for many years and knows this abuse thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu said, "I presided over appointments for many years and know this abuse well.

sentences.zh: 今寰區未復，員闕不多。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet restored and vacant posts are not numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The empire is not yet recovered, and vacant posts are still few.

sentences.zh: 若總無條綱，恐難持久。

translations.literal: If there are no rules at all, I fear this cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: If we have no standards at all, I fear the practice cannot last.

sentences.zh: 」上然之，未暇厘革。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed but had no leisure to reform the system.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed but had no time yet to reform the system.

sentences.zh: 及還京，選人數千，補授無所，喧訴於朝，由是行見素之言。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital thousands of candidates had no posts to which they could be appointed and clamored in protest at court; because of this Jiansu's advice was put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to the capital thousands of candidates had no posts to fill and protested loudly at court, and Jiansu's advice was finally adopted.

sentences.zh: 及房琯以敗軍左降，崔圓、崔渙等皆罷知政事，上皇所命宰臣，無知政事者。

translations.literal: When Fang Guan was demoted to the left for military defeat and Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, and others were all removed from participation in government, among the chief ministers appointed by the Retired Emperor none remained in charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Guan was demoted after his military defeat and Cui Yuan, Cui Huan, and others were removed from office, none of the chief ministers appointed by the retired emperor still held real power.

sentences.zh: 五月，遷見素太子太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jiansu was transferred to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jiansu was made grand preceptor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十一月，肅宗自右輔還京，詔見素入蜀奉迎太上皇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, when Suzong returned to the capital from the western capital region, he ordered Jiansu to enter Shu to escort the Retired Emperor back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, when Suzong returned to the capital from the western capital, he ordered Jiansu into Shu to escort the retired emperor home.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上皇至京師，肅宗禦樓大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Retired Emperor reached the capital and Suzong proclaimed a great amnesty from the palace tower.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the retired emperor reached the capital, and Suzong proclaimed a general amnesty from the palace tower.

sentences.zh: 見素以奉上皇幸蜀功，加開府儀同三司，食實封三百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in escorting the Retired Emperor on the tour to Shu, Jiansu was given the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上元中，以足疾上表請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era, citing illness of the feet, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was permitted to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era he petitioned to retire on account of a foot ailment, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年十二月卒，年七十六，贈司空，謚曰忠貞，喪事官給。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoying he died at the age of seventy-six; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his funeral expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of Baoying 1 at the age of seventy-six. He was posthumously made minister of works, given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his funeral was paid for by the state.

sentences.zh: 子倜、諤、益、丱。

translations.literal: His sons were Ti, E, Yi, and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ti, E, Yi, and Guan.

sentences.zh: 倜、諤皆位至給事中，益終刑部員外郎，丱終秘書丞。

translations.literal: Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ti and E both rose to Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as a vice-director in the ministry of justice, and Guan as a secretary in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 倜子頌。

translations.literal: Ti's son was Song.
translations.idiomatic: Ti had a son named Song.

sentences.zh: 益子顗，字周人，生一歲而孤，事姊稱為恭孝。

translations.literal: Yi's son Yan, courtesy name Zhouren, was orphaned at the age of one; in serving his elder sister he was praised as reverent and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Yan, courtesy name Zhouren, lost his father when he was only one year old and was known for the reverent care he gave his elder sister.

sentences.zh: 性嗜學，尤精陰陽、象緯、經略、風俗之書。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning and was especially expert in books on yin and yang, astral signs, statecraft, and local customs.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was especially versed in works on cosmology, astronomy, statecraft, and regional customs.

sentences.zh: 善持論，有清譽。

translations.literal: He was skilled in debate and enjoyed a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He argued persuasively and enjoyed a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 少以門廕補千牛備身，自鄠縣尉判入等，授萬年尉，歷御史、補闕、尚書郎，累遷給事中、尚書左丞、戶部侍郎、中丞、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; from his evaluation as district magistrate of E he was graded for appointment and made magistrate of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After a favorable evaluation as magistrate of E County he was appointed magistrate of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 其在諫垣，與李約、李正辭叠申裨諷，頗回大政。

translations.literal: While in the remonstrance bureau he joined Li Yue and Li Zhengchen in repeatedly offering corrective admonitions and greatly influenced major policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the remonstrance bureau he joined Li Yue and Li Zhengchen in repeated memorials of admonition and helped shape major policy decisions.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴垍、李絳、崔群輩多與友善，而後進之有浮名者，亦遊其門，以是稱有時望。

translations.literal: Chief ministers such as Pei Ji, Li Jiang, and Cui Qun were largely on friendly terms with him, and younger men with inflated reputations also frequented his gate; for this he was said to enjoy contemporary esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with chief ministers such as Pei Ji, Li Jiang, and Cui Qun, and younger men seeking reputation also sought his patronage, which gave him standing among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 及李逢吉殲朋黨以專政柄，而顗附麗之跡尤密，頗為時人所譏。

translations.literal: When Li Fengji destroyed factional groups to monopolize power, Yan's traces of attachment to him were especially close, and he was much ridiculed by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fengji destroyed the factions to monopolize power, Yan clung to him more closely than ever and was widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 然處身儉約，有足多者。

translations.literal: Yet in his personal conduct he was frugal and restrained, and there was much to praise in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lived frugally, and in that respect he was genuinely admirable.

sentences.zh: 著《易蘊解》，推演潛亢終始之義，甚有奧旨。

translations.literal: He wrote Explication of the Stored Meaning of the Changes, expounding the principles of hidden and manifest, beginning and end, with very profound intent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Explication of the Stored Meaning of the Changes, developing the Book of Changes' themes of hidden and manifest, beginning and end, with real depth.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年七月卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Baoli he died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Baoli 1 and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 崔圓，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 後魏左僕射亮之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Cui Liang, left vice-director of the Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Cui Liang, who had been left vice-director under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父景晊，官至大理評事。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi reached the post of judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzhi rose to the post of judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 圓少孤貧，誌尚閎博，好讀兵書，有經濟宇宙之心。

translations.literal: Yuan was orphaned and poor in youth; his aspirations were broad and lofty, he loved to read books of war, and he harbored a mind to order the universe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was orphaned and poor as a youth, but his ambitions were vast. He loved military texts and dreamed of governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 開元中，詔搜訪遺逸，圓以鈐謀射策甲科，授執戟。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era an edict sought out hidden talents; Yuan passed the military-strategy examination in the top grade and was appointed armed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan the court sought out neglected talent; Yuan took top honors in the military-strategy examination and was appointed an armed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 自負文藝，獲武職，頗不得意。

translations.literal: Proud of his literary talent yet given a military post, he was quite discontent.
translations.idiomatic: He took pride in his literary gifts but had been given a military post, and he was deeply dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 蕭炅為京兆尹，薦為會昌丞，累遷司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: When Xiao Jiong was Jingzhao intendant he recommended Yuan as assistant magistrate of Huichang, and Yuan was promoted repeatedly to vice-director in the Ministry of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Jiong became Jingzhao intendant he recommended Yuan as assistant magistrate of Huichang, and Yuan rose to vice-director in the Ministry of Honors.

sentences.zh: 宰臣楊國忠遙制劍南節度使，引圓佐理，乃奏授尚書郎，兼蜀郡大都督府左司馬，知節度留後。

translations.literal: Chief minister Yang Guozhong controlled the Jiannan military governor from afar and brought Yuan in to assist in administration; he memorialized to appoint him a director in the Secretariat, with concurrent post as left military aide in the Shu metropolitan prefecture and charge of the military governor's rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Yang Guozhong controlled Jiannan from the capital and brought Yuan in to help run the circuit. He had Yuan appointed a secretariat director, made him left military aide in the Shu metropolitan government, and put him in charge of rear affairs for the military governorship.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，玄宗幸蜀郡，特遷蜀郡大都督府長史、劍南節度。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, when Emperor Xuanzong toured Shu Prefecture, Yuan was specially promoted to chief administrator of the Shu metropolitan prefecture and military governor of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, when Xuanzong fled to Shu, Yuan was promoted to chief administrator of the Shu metropolitan prefecture and military governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 圓素懷功名，初聞國難，潛使人探國忠深旨，知有行幸之計，乃增修城池，建置館宇，儲備什器。

translations.literal: Yuan had long coveted fame and achievement; when he first heard of the national crisis he secretly sent men to probe Guozhong's deeper intentions, learned of the plan for an imperial tour, and then enlarged and repaired the city walls, built lodges and halls, and stored equipment and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had long sought fame. When rebellion broke out he secretly learned from Guozhong's circle that the emperor meant to flee to Shu, and he hastened to repair the walls, build lodges, and stock supplies for the imperial arrival.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿至，殿宇牙帳咸如宿設，玄宗甚嗟賞之，即日拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、劍南節度，余如故。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, the halls and military tents were all as if long prepared; Emperor Xuanzong greatly admired this and that same day appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and military governor of Jiannan, with other duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, the halls and camp were ready as though prepared long in advance. Xuanzong was deeply impressed and that same day made Yuan vice director of the secretariat, grand councilor, and military governor of Jiannan, with his other duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，玄宗命圓同房琯、韋見素並赴肅宗行在所，玄宗親制遺愛碑於蜀以寵之。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, Xuanzong ordered Yuan to go with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to Suzong's traveling court; Xuanzong personally composed a stele of enduring affection in Shu to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, the retired emperor sent Yuan with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to Suzong's court and personally composed a stele praising Yuan's service in Shu.

sentences.zh: 從肅宗還京，以功拜中書令，封趙國公，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Following Suzong back to the capital, for his merit he was appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and granted an actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied Suzong back to the capital he was made director of the secretariat, created Duke of Zhao, and granted a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷知政事，遷太子少師，留守東都。

translations.literal: The following year he ceased participation in government, was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and remained to guard the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he left office, became junior tutor of the crown prince, and was left to guard the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 會官軍不利於相州，軍回過洛陽，所在剽掠。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial army met defeat at Xiang Prefecture; as the troops returned through Luoyang they plundered wherever they passed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army was defeated at Xiang Prefecture, the retreating troops passed through Luoyang and plundered the countryside.

sentences.zh: 圓棄城南奔襄陽，詔削除階封。

translations.literal: Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang; an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.

sentences.zh: 尋起為濟王傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as tutor to the Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as tutor to the Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 李光弼用為懷州刺史，除太子詹事，改汾州刺史，皆以理行稱。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi employed him as prefect of Huai; he was appointed steward of the crown prince, then transferred to prefect of Fen, and in each post was praised for orderly conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi appointed him prefect of Huai. He later served as steward of the crown prince and then prefect of Fen, earning praise for good governance in each post.

sentences.zh: 拜揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度觀察使，加檢校右僕射、兼御史大夫，轉檢校左僕射知省事。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture and military governor and observer of Huainan, given the acting title of right vice-director and concurrent post as censor-in-chief, then transferred to acting left vice-director with charge of secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief administrator of Yangzhou and military governor of Huainan, given the acting rank of right vice-director with the concurrent post of censor-in-chief, and later became acting left vice-director in charge of secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年六月薨，年六十四，輟朝三日，贈太子太師，謚曰昭襄。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Dali he died at the age of sixty-four; court mourning was observed for three days; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince with the posthumous title Illustrious and Assisting.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Dali 3 at the age of sixty-four. Court was suspended for three days of mourning. He was posthumously made grand preceptor of the crown prince and given the posthumous title Illustrious and Assisting.

sentences.zh: 崔渙，祖玄暐，神龍功臣，封博陵郡王。

translations.literal: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei was a meritorious servant of the Shenlong coup and was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei had been ennobled as Duke of Boling for his service in the Shenlong coup.

sentences.zh: 父璩，文學知名，位至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Zhang was renowned for literary learning and reached the post of vice-minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang was a noted scholar who rose to vice-minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 渙少以士行聞，博綜經籍，尤善談論，累遷尚書司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Huan was known from youth for conduct befitting a gentleman; he mastered the classics broadly and was especially skilled in discourse, and was promoted repeatedly to vice-director of the Gate Office in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was known from youth for his integrity, mastered the classics, and was an accomplished speaker. He rose to vice-director of the Gate Office in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠出不附己者，渙出為劍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Yang Guozhong removed those who did not support him, and Huan was sent out as prefect of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, Yang Guozhong banished those who would not support him, and Huan was sent out as prefect of Jian.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載七月，玄宗幸蜀，渙迎謁於路，抗詞忠懇，皆究理體，玄宗嘉之，以為得渙晚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Xuanzong toured Shu, Huan met and greeted him on the road with loyal and earnest words that all penetrated to the root of principle; the emperor praised him and felt he had found Huan too late.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianbao 15, when Xuanzong fled to Shu, Huan met him on the road with loyal, forceful counsel that went to the heart of the crisis. The emperor praised him and regretted that he had not found him sooner.

sentences.zh: 宰臣房琯又薦之，即日拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，扈從成都府。

translations.literal: Chief minister Fang Guan also recommended him, and that same day he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, escorting the court to Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Fang Guan also recommended him, and that same day he was made vice director of the chancellery and grand councilor, accompanying the court to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗靈武即位。

translations.literal: Suzong took the throne at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong ascended the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 八月，與左相韋見素、同平章事房琯、崔圓同賫冊赴行在。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he went with left chancellor Wei Jiansu, Grand Councilor Fang Guan, and Cui Yuan to carry the investiture registers to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he went with left chancellor Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, and Cui Yuan to deliver the investiture registers to Suzong's court.

sentences.zh: 時未復京師，舉選路絕，詔渙充江淮宣諭選補使，以收遺逸。

translations.literal: The capital had not yet been recovered and the routes for examinations and selection were cut off; Huan was ordered to serve as commissioner to proclaim and select candidates in Jiang-Huai to gather neglected talent.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital still unreclaimed and the examination routes cut off, Huan was appointed commissioner to recruit and appoint officials in the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 惑於聽受，為下吏所鬻，濫進者非一，以不稱職聞。

translations.literal: Misled in what he heard and accepted, he was sold out by subordinate officials, and improper appointments were not few; he became known as unfit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was misled by what he was told and deceived by his subordinates, and many unqualified men were appointed. He soon gained a reputation for incompetence.

sentences.zh: 乃罷知政事，除左散騎常侍，兼余杭太守、江東采訪防禦使。

translations.literal: He was then removed from participation in government, appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace, and given concurrent posts as prefect of Yuhang and Jiangdong investigation and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office and made left regular attendant of the palace, with concurrent posts as prefect of Yuhang and Jiangdong investigation and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 旋授正議大夫、太子賓客。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the title Grand Master of Correct Counsel and appointed guest of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the title Grand Master of Correct Counsel and appointed a guest of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年正月，轉大理卿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Qianyuan he was transferred to director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianyuan 3 he was made director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部侍郎、檢校工部尚書、集賢院待詔。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to vice-minister of personnel, acting minister of works, and awaiting imperial orders at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to vice-minister of personnel, acting minister of works, and scholar awaiting orders at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 性尚簡淡，不交世務，頗為時望所歸。

translations.literal: By nature he favored simplicity and detachment and did not mingle in worldly affairs, and contemporary esteem largely turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply, avoided worldly entanglements, and enjoyed wide respect among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫，加稅地青苗錢物使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor-in-chief and given the additional post of commissioner for green-sprout tax money and goods on taxed land.
translations.idiomatic: He was made censor-in-chief and also appointed commissioner for the green-sprout land tax.

sentences.zh: 時以此錢充給京百官料，渙為屬吏希中，以下估為使料，上估為百官料。

translations.literal: At that time this money was used to supply the salaries of capital officials; Huan, to please his subordinates, used the low valuation for his commissioner's funds and the high valuation for officials' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The tax was meant to fund salaries for capital officials, but Huan, currying favor with his staff, used low valuations for his own commissioner's funds and high valuations for the officials' pay.

sentences.zh: 其時為皇城副留守張清發之，詔下有司訊鞫，渙無詞以對，坐是貶道州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Guardian of the Imperial City Zhang Qing exposed the matter; an edict ordered the relevant offices to investigate and interrogate; Huan had no words with which to reply and for this was demoted to prefect of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Vice guardian of the imperial city Zhang Qing exposed the fraud. When officials investigated, Huan had no defense and was demoted to prefect of Dao.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年十二月壬寅，以疾終。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the twelfth month of the third year of Dali he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness on the renyin day of the twelfth month of Dali 3.

sentences.zh: 子縱，初以廕補協律郎，三遷為監察御史。

translations.literal: His son Zong first entered office by hereditary privilege as harmonics officer, and after three promotions became investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong entered office by hereditary privilege as a harmonics officer and after three promotions became an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 詔擇令長於臺省，除藍田令，寬明勤幹，德化大行，縣人為之立碑頌德。

translations.literal: An edict selected district magistrates from the central offices; he was appointed magistrate of Lantian, where he was broad-minded, clear, diligent, and capable, and moral transformation was greatly carried out; the people of the district erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the court chose district magistrates from the central offices he was appointed magistrate of Lantian. He governed with clarity and energy, won the people's trust, and they erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 轉京兆府司錄，累遷金部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to recording officer in the Jingzhao prefectural staff and was promoted repeatedly to vice-director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became recording officer in the Jingzhao prefectural staff and rose to vice-director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以父貶道州刺史，棄官就養。

translations.literal: When his father was demoted to prefect of Dao he abandoned his office to go and support him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was demoted to prefect of Dao he resigned his post to care for him.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，終制，六遷大理卿、兼御史中丞、汴西水陸運兩稅鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning; when the mourning period was completed he was promoted six times to director of the Court of Judicial Review, with concurrent posts as vice censor-in-chief and commissioner for Bianxi water-and-land transport, two-tax, and salt-and-iron affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and when it ended he rose through six promotions to director of the Court of Judicial Review, with concurrent posts as vice censor-in-chief and commissioner for Bianxi transport, the two-tax system, and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 田悅連敗，走魏州，嬰城自守，諸道兵圍之，屢乏食，詔縱兼魏州四節度糧料使，軍儲稍給。

translations.literal: Tian Yue suffered repeated defeats, fled to Wei Prefecture, and held the city in defense; troops from various circuits besieged him and food was often lacking; Zong was ordered to serve concurrently as grain commissioner for the four military governors around Wei, and army provisions were gradually supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was repeatedly defeated and fled to Wei Prefecture, where he held the city under siege. Food ran short for the besieging armies, and Zong was appointed grain commissioner for the four circuits around Wei, gradually restoring supplies.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，四方握兵，未有至者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong toured Fengtian, those holding troops in the four directions had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong fled to Fengtian, none of the regional commanders holding troops had yet reached him.

sentences.zh: 縱先知之，潛告李懷光勸令奔命，懷光從之。

translations.literal: Zong learned of it beforehand and secretly told Li Huaiguang, urging him to hurry to the emperor's call; Huaiguang followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zong learned of the crisis first and secretly urged Li Huaiguang to march to the emperor's aid, and Huaiguang agreed.

sentences.zh: 縱乃悉斂軍財與懷光俱來，調給具備。

translations.literal: Zong then gathered all military funds and came with Huaiguang, with supplies fully arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Zong gathered all military funds and marched with Huaiguang, bringing full supplies for the relief force.

sentences.zh: 懷光兵士久戰河外，及次河中，將遷延。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's soldiers had long fought east of the Yellow River, and when they halted at Hezhong they were about to delay.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's troops had fought long east of the Yellow River, and when they reached Hezhong they were ready to halt.

sentences.zh: 縱之貨幣先已渡河，縱謂眾曰：「若濟，悉以分賜。

translations.literal: Zong's money and goods had already crossed the river beforehand; Zong said to the troops, "If we cross, I will distribute it all among you.
translations.idiomatic: Zong had already sent his funds across the river. He told the troops, "If we cross now, I will divide it all among you.

sentences.zh: 」眾利之，乃西。

translations.literal: " The troops were pleased by this and then marched west.
translations.idiomatic: " The promise won them over, and they marched west.

sentences.zh: 至奉天，加右庶子，充使。

translations.literal: When they reached Fengtian he was given the additional post of right assistant to the heir apparent and made commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian he was made right assistant to the heir apparent and appointed a commissioner.

sentences.zh: 無幾，拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Jingzhao intendant with concurrent post as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Jingzhao intendant with the concurrent post of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 數奏懷光剛愎反覆，宜陰備之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Huaiguang was obstinate and changeable and should be secretly guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly warned that Huaiguang was obstinate and untrustworthy and should be watched in secret.

sentences.zh: 及行幸梁州，左右或短之曰：「縱素善懷光，今不來矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured Liang Prefecture, those around him sometimes slandered Zong, saying, "Zong has long been on good terms with Huaiguang; he will not come now.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Liang Prefecture, some at court whispered, "Zong has always been close to Huaiguang; he will not come now.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「他人不知縱，吾可保其心。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Others do not know Zong as I do; I can vouch for his heart.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "Others do not know Zong as I do. I can trust his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」不數日，縱至，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: " Within a few days Zong arrived and was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: " Within a few days Zong arrived and was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗議其大體，不親細事，獄訴儀制，皆付之僚吏。

translations.literal: He would discuss only the larger principles and did not attend to small matters; lawsuits, ritual, and regulations were all entrusted to his subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: He concerned himself only with broad policy and left lawsuits, ritual, and routine business to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 縱孝悌，修飭自立，以父為元載排抑，居退十餘年，左宦外府，訖載得罪，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Zong was filial and brotherly, disciplined himself and stood on his own; because his father had been suppressed by Yuan Zai he lived in retirement for more than ten years, serving in demoted posts in outer prefectures until Zai fell from power, and did not seek fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was filial and self-disciplined. After his father was ruined by Yuan Zai he lived in retirement for more than ten years in minor posts in the provinces and sought no advancement until Zai fell.

sentences.zh: 初，渙有寵妾鄭氏，縱以母事之。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan had a favored concubine, Lady Zheng, whom Zong treated as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had once had a favored concubine, Lady Zheng, whom Zong treated as his mother.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏性剛戾，待縱不以理，雖為大僚，每加笞詬。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng was by nature harsh and perverse and did not treat Zong according to reason; though he was a high official she often beat and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng was harsh and unreasonable. Though Zong had risen to high office, she still beat and scolded him.

sentences.zh: 縱率妻子候顏，敬順不懈，時以為難。

translations.literal: Zong led his wife and children to attend her countenance with reverent obedience without slackening, and men of the time regarded this as difficult to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Zong brought his wife and children to wait on her with unwavering respect, and contemporaries considered this a rare feat of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 杜鴻漸，故相暹之族子。

translations.literal: Du Hongjian was a clansman of the former chancellor Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hongjian was a kinsman of the former chancellor Du Xian.

sentences.zh: 祖慎行，益州長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenxing was chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenxing had been chief administrator of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父鵬舉，官至王友。

translations.literal: His father Pengju reached the post of companion to a prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pengju rose to the post of companion to a prince.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸敏悟好學，舉進士，解褐王府參軍。

translations.literal: Hongjian was quick-witted and loved learning; he passed the jinshi examination and left commoner status as a staff officer in a princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was quick-witted and studious. He passed the jinshi examination and took his first post as a staff officer in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，累遷大理司直，朔方留後、支度副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was promoted repeatedly to judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, rear commissioner of Shuofang, and deputy commissioner for supplies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he rose to judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, rear commissioner of Shuofang, and deputy commissioner for supplies.

sentences.zh: 肅宗北幸，至平涼，未知所適。

translations.literal: When Suzong toured north and reached Pingliang, he did not know where to go next.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong marched north and reached Pingliang, he did not know which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸與六城水運使魏少遊、節度判官崔漪、支度判官盧簡金、關內鹽池判官李涵謀曰：「今胡羯亂常，二京陷沒，主上南幸於巴蜀，皇太子理兵於平涼。

translations.literal: Hongjian plotted with Wei Shaoyou, commissioner for the Six Cities water transport, the military governor's aide Cui Yi, the supplies aide Lu Jianjin, and the Guannei salt-pond aide Li Han, saying, "Now the barbarian rebels have thrown the realm into chaos; the two capitals have fallen; the sovereign has toured south to Ba-Shu, and the Crown Prince is organizing troops at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian conferred with Wei Shaoyou, commissioner for the Six Cities water transport, military governor's aide Cui Yi, supplies aide Lu Jianjin, and Guannei salt-pond aide Li Han. He said, "The barbarian rebels have thrown the realm into chaos. Both capitals have fallen. The emperor has fled south to Ba-Shu, and the crown prince is gathering troops at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 然平涼散地，非聚兵之處，必欲制勝，非朔方不可。

translations.literal: Yet Pingliang is open country and not a place to concentrate troops; if we wish to gain victory, we cannot do without Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: But Pingliang is open country, not a place to mass an army. If we mean to win, we must have Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 若奉殿下，旬日之間，西收河、隴，回紇方強，與國通好，北征勁騎，南集諸城，大兵一舉，可復二京。

translations.literal: If we escort Your Highness, within ten days we can recover He-Long in the west; the Uyghurs are now strong and on friendly terms with the state; with fierce northern cavalry and southern concentration of the walled cities, one great campaign can recover the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: If we escort Your Highness to Shuofang, within days we can recover the northwest. The Uyghurs are strong and friendly; with their cavalry from the north and our southern garrisons united, one campaign can retake both capitals.

sentences.zh: 雪社稷之恥，上報明主，下安蒼生，亦臣子之用心，國家之大計也。

translations.literal: To wipe away the shame of the altars of state, repay the enlightened sovereign above, and settle the common people below is likewise the mind of a loyal subject and the great plan of the state.
translations.idiomatic: To wipe away the shame of the dynasty, serve the emperor, and bring peace to the people is both a subject's duty and the state's greatest need.

sentences.zh: 」鴻漸即日草箋具陳兵馬招集之勢，錄軍資、器械、倉儲、庫物之數，令李涵賫赴平涼，肅宗大悅。

translations.literal: " That same day Hongjian drafted a memorial fully setting forth the situation for gathering troops and horses, recorded the numbers of military funds, weapons, granaries, and storehouse goods, and had Li Han carry it to Pingliang; Suzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Hongjian drafted a detailed report on troop strength and listed all military funds, weapons, and stores, sending Li Han to Pingliang with it. Suzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸知肅宗發平涼，於北界白草頓迎謁，因勞諸使及兵士，進言曰：「朔方天下勁兵，靈州用武之處。

translations.literal: When Hongjian learned that Suzong had set out from Pingliang, he met and greeted him at Baicao Station on the northern border, consoled the various commissioners and soldiers, and advanced the argument, "Shuofang has the strongest troops under heaven; Ling Prefecture is the place for wielding arms.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Suzong had left Pingliang, Hongjian met him at Baicao Station on the northern frontier, thanked the commissioners and troops, and urged, "Shuofang has the finest troops in the empire. Ling Prefecture is the true base for war.

sentences.zh: 今回紇請和，吐蕃內附，天下郡邑，人皆堅守，以待制命。

translations.literal: Now the Uyghurs seek peace and Tibet has submitted within; in prefectures and districts throughout the realm people all hold firm and await imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs seek peace and Tibet has submitted. Throughout the empire the people hold their cities and await your orders.

sentences.zh: 其中雖為賊所據，亦望不日收復，殿下整理軍戎，長驅一舉，則逆胡不足滅也。

translations.literal: Though some among them are held by the rebels, they too hope to be recovered before long; if Your Highness puts the army in order and drives forward in one thrust, the rebellious barbarians are not enough to destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Even those now held by the rebels can be recovered soon. If Your Highness organizes the army and strikes in one thrust, the rebels cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗然之。

translations.literal: " Suzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Suzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 及至靈武，鴻漸與裴冕等勸即皇帝位，以歸中外之望，五上表，乃從。

translations.literal: When they reached Lingwu, Hongjian with Pei Mian and others urged him to take the imperial throne immediately to answer the hopes within and without; after five memorials he at last assented.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu, Hongjian and Pei Mian urged him to take the throne at once to satisfy the hopes of the court and the realm. After five memorials Suzong finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸素習帝王陳布之儀，君臣朝見之禮，遂采摭舊儀，綿蕝其事。

translations.literal: Hongjian had long been versed in the ceremonies by which emperors set forth their rule and the rites of court audience between ruler and minister; he therefore gathered old protocols and laid out the matter in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was well versed in imperial ceremony and court ritual. He gathered the old protocols and arranged the enthronement rites in full.

sentences.zh: 城南設壇壝，先一日具儀註草奏。

translations.literal: South of the city they set up an altar and enclosure; one day beforehand he prepared the ritual notes and drafted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: They set up an altar south of the city, and the day before he prepared the ritual notes and draft memorial.

sentences.zh: 肅宗曰：「聖君在遠，寇逆未平，宜罷壇場。

translations.literal: Suzong said, "The sage sovereign is far away and the rebels are not yet pacified; the altar rites should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong said, "The emperor is still far away and the rebels are not yet defeated. The altar ceremony should be canceled.

sentences.zh: 」余可其奏。

translations.literal: " The rest of the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rest of the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，授兵部郎中，知中書舍人事，尋轉武部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne he was appointed director in the Ministry of War with charge of Secretariat drafter affairs, and soon transferred to vice-minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne he was made director in the Ministry of War with charge of secretariat drafting, and soon became vice-minister of war.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，兼御史大夫，為河西節度使、涼州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was given concurrent post as censor-in-chief and made military governor of Hexi and protector-general of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 he was also made censor-in-chief and appointed military governor of Hexi and protector-general of Liang.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，遷荊州大都督府長史、荊南節度使。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified he was transferred to chief administrator of the Jingzhou metropolitan prefecture and military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals were recovered he was made chief administrator of Jingzhou and military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 襄州大將康楚元、張嘉延盜所管兵，據襄州城叛，刺史王政遁走。

translations.literal: The great generals of Xiang Prefecture Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan stole the troops under their command, seized Xiang Prefecture city in rebellion, and the prefect Wang Zheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Prefecture generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan seized the troops under their command, rebelled, and occupied Xiang city while the prefect Wang Zheng fled.

sentences.zh: 嘉延南襲荊州，鴻漸聞之，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Jiayan attacked south toward Jing Prefecture; when Hongjian heard of it he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayan marched south against Jing Prefecture. When Hongjian heard of it he abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 澧、朗、硤、歸等州聞鴻漸出奔，皆惶駭，潛竄山谷。

translations.literal: When the prefectures of Li, Lang, Xia, and Gui heard that Hongjian had fled, all were terrified and secretly hid in the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectures of Li, Lang, Xia, and Gui heard that Hongjian had fled, the people panicked and hid in the hills.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徵拜尚書右丞、吏部侍郎、太常卿，充禮儀使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed right vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and made commissioner of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was recalled as right vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed commissioner of ritual.

sentences.zh: 二聖晏駕，鴻漸監護儀制，山陵畢，加光祿大夫，封衛國公。

translations.literal: When the two sage emperors passed away Hongjian supervised the ritual protocols; when the imperial tombs were completed he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Blessing and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When both emperors died Hongjian supervised the funeral rites. After the burials were completed he was made Grand Master of Splendid Blessing and created Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，代宗將享郊廟，拜鴻漸兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，尋轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, when Emperor Daizong was about to offer at the suburban altars, Hongjian was appointed vice-minister of war and Grand Councilor, and soon transferred to vice-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 2, when Daizong was to perform the suburban sacrifices, Hongjian was made vice-minister of war and grand councilor, and soon became vice-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年十月，劍南西川兵馬使崔旰殺節度使郭英乂，據成都，自稱留後。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongtai, Cui Han, military commissioner of Jiannan West, killed the military governor Guo Yingyi, seized Chengdu, and styled himself rear commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongtai 1, Jiannan West military commissioner Cui Han killed military governor Guo Yingyi, seized Chengdu, and declared himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 邛州衙將柏貞節、瀘州衙將楊子琳、劍州衙將李昌巙等興兵討旰，西蜀大亂。

translations.literal: The yamen generals Bo Zhenjie of Qiong, Yang Zilin of Lu, and Li Changchong of Jian and others raised troops to attack Han, and western Shu fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen generals Bo Zhenjie of Qiong, Yang Zilin of Lu, and Li Changchong of Jian raised armies against Han, and western Shu descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，命鴻漸以宰相兼充山、劍副元帥、劍南西川節度使，以平蜀亂。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Hongjian was ordered, as chief minister, to serve concurrently as deputy commander of the Shan and Jian armies and military governor of Jiannan West to pacify the Shu rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The following February he was sent as chief minister and deputy commander of the Shan and Jian armies and military governor of Jiannan West to suppress the rebellion in Shu.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸心無遠圖，志氣怯懦，又酷好浮圖道，不喜軍戎。

translations.literal: Hongjian had no far-reaching plans in his heart, his spirit was timid and weak, and he was passionately devoted to Buddhism and disliked military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian lacked strategic vision, was timid by nature, was passionately devoted to Buddhism, and disliked military affairs.

sentences.zh: 既至成都，懼旰雄武，不復問罪，乃以劍南節制表讓於旰。

translations.literal: When he reached Chengdu he feared Han's martial prowess, no longer pressed charges against him, and submitted a memorial yielding control of Jiannan to Han.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chengdu he feared Han's power, made no move to punish him, and submitted a memorial yielding control of Jiannan to Han.

sentences.zh: 時西戎寇邊，關中多事，鴻漸孤軍陷險，兵威不振，代宗不獲已，從之。

translations.literal: At that time the western barbarians raided the borders and Guanzhong was beset with troubles; Hongjian's isolated army was trapped in danger and military prestige did not rise; Daizong, having no choice, assented.
translations.idiomatic: Western tribes were raiding the frontier and Guanzhong was in turmoil. Hongjian's isolated army was in peril and could not prevail. Daizong had no choice but to agree.

sentences.zh: 仍以旰為劍南西川行軍司馬，柏貞節為邛州刺史，楊子琳為瀘州刺史，各罷兵。

translations.literal: Han was still appointed campaigning marshal of Jiannan West, Bo Zhenjie prefect of Qiong, and Yang Zilin prefect of Lu, and each disbanded his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Han was confirmed as campaigning marshal of Jiannan West, Bo Zhenjie as prefect of Qiong, and Yang Zilin as prefect of Lu, and each army stood down.

sentences.zh: 尋請入覲，仍表崔旰為西川兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Soon he requested permission to come to court and again memorialized to make Cui Han rear military commissioner of western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to court and memorialized again to confirm Cui Han as acting military commissioner of western Shu.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年，詔以旰為成都尹、劍南西川節度使，召鴻漸還京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali an edict appointed Han intendant of Chengdu and military governor of Jiannan West and recalled Hongjian to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 2 an edict made Han intendant of Chengdu and military governor of Jiannan West and recalled Hongjian to the capital.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸仍率旰同入覲，代宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Hongjian still led Han to enter court together for an audience, and Daizong praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian brought Han to court with him for an audience, and Daizong commended the gesture.

sentences.zh: 後知政事，轉門下侍郎，讓山南副元帥。

translations.literal: Later he participated in government, was transferred to vice-director of the Chancellery, and yielded the post of deputy commander of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to government, became vice-director of the chancellery, and relinquished the deputy command of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，代王縉為東都留守，充河南、淮西、山南東道副元帥，平章事如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, became deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, and retained his grand councilorship.

sentences.zh: 以疾上表乞骸骨，從之，竟不之任。

translations.literal: Because of illness he submitted a memorial requesting to retire with his old bones; his request was granted, and in the end he never took up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to petition for retirement; the request was granted, and he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月卒，贈太尉，謚曰文憲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he died; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and given the posthumous title Cultured and Lawful.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of the fourth year and was posthumously made grand marshal with the posthumous title Cultured and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 輟朝三日，賜物五百疋，粟五百石。

translations.literal: Court mourning was observed for three days, and five hundred bolts of goods and five hundred shi of grain were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days of mourning, and he was granted five hundred bolts of goods and five hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸晚年樂於退靜，私第在長興裏，館宇華靡，賓僚宴集。

translations.literal: In his later years Hongjian delighted in retirement and quiet; his private residence was in Changxing Ward, its halls and lodges lavish, and guests and staff gathered for feasts.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Hongjian enjoyed retirement. His home in Changxing Ward was lavish, and he entertained guests and staff there.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸悠然賦詩曰：「常願追禪理，安能挹化源。

translations.literal: Hongjian composed a poem at leisure, saying, "I have long wished to pursue the principles of Chan; how could I draw from the source of transformation?
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian wrote a poem in a tranquil mood: "I have long wished to follow the way of Chan; how could I drink from the source of transformation?

sentences.zh: 」朝士多屬和之。

translations.literal: " Many court officials wrote matching verses.
translations.idiomatic: " Many court officials wrote matching verses in reply.

sentences.zh: 及休致後病，令僧剃頂發，及卒，遺命其子依胡法塔葬，不為封樹，冀類緇流，物議哂之。

translations.literal: When after retirement he fell ill he had monks shave his crown; when he died he left instructions to his sons to bury him according to the foreign Buddhist method in a pagoda, without a mound or trees, hoping to be classed with the black-robed clergy; public opinion ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired he fell ill and had monks shave his head. At his death he ordered his sons to bury him in a Buddhist pagoda without a mound or trees, hoping to be counted among the clergy. Public opinion mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：祿山狂悖已顯，玄宗寵任無疑，見素知國危，陳廟算，直言極諫，而君不從，獨正犯難，而人不咎，出生入死，善始令終者鮮矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lushan's madness and rebellion were already manifest, and Emperor Xuanzong's favor and trust were beyond doubt. Jiansu knew the state was in peril, set forth plans for the altars of state, and remonstrated with utmost directness, yet the ruler would not follow; he alone upheld rectitude in facing calamity, yet men did not blame him — those who pass through life and death with a good beginning and a fine end are few.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: An Lushan's treachery was already plain, and Xuanzong's favor was beyond question. Jiansu saw the danger, laid out plans for the dynasty, and remonstrated boldly, yet the emperor would not listen. He alone upheld what was right through the crisis, and men did not blame him. Few pass through such trials with honor from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 時論以見素取容於國忠，無言匡大政。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Jiansu sought to please Guozhong and did not speak to correct great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said Jiansu had curried favor with Guozhong and failed to speak out on great matters of state.

sentences.zh: 且國忠恃內戚，弄重權，沮林甫奸豪，取其大位，若見素之孤直，豈許取容？

translations.literal: Moreover Guozhong relied on his kinship with the inner court, wielded heavy power, blocked the villainous prowess of Li Linfu, and seized his great position — would one as upright and solitary as Jiansu have been allowed to seek favor?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Guozhong relied on imperial kinship, wielded enormous power, and displaced the powerful Li Linfu. Would a man as upright and independent as Jiansu have been permitted merely to flatter him?

sentences.zh: 蓋禍胎已成，政柄久紊，見素入相余年，言不從而難作，雖有周、孔之才，其能匡救者乎？

translations.literal: The womb of disaster had already formed and the handles of government had long been in disorder; Jiansu entered the chancellorship for more than a year, his words were not followed, and calamity arose — even with the talents of the Duke of Zhou or Confucius, could he have rescued the state?
translations.idiomatic: The seeds of disaster were already sown and government had long been corrupt. Jiansu served as chief minister for more than a year, but his counsel went unheeded and catastrophe followed. Even a man with the talents of the Duke of Zhou or Confucius could not have saved the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 諤才辯，顗儉約，雅符積善之慶矣。

translations.literal: E was talented in debate and Yan frugal and restrained — they finely matched the blessing of accumulated goodness.
translations.idiomatic: E was gifted in debate and Yan lived frugally — fitting rewards for a family that had accumulated virtue.

sentences.zh: 圓守文之士，非禦侮之才。

translations.literal: Yuan was a man who upheld written norms, not one with talent to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a man of routine administration, not a defender against calamity.

sentences.zh: 渙才兼行聞，命與時會。

translations.literal: Huan's talent and conduct were both renowned; his fate met the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was known for both talent and integrity, and his rise matched the times.

sentences.zh: 發言上沃主意，遽致顯榮；

translations.literal: In speaking he enriched the sovereign's intent above and swiftly attained conspicuous honor;
translations.idiomatic: His words won the emperor's heart and brought him swift advancement;

sentences.zh: 當官屢為吏欺，終及竄逐。

translations.literal: in office he was repeatedly deceived by subordinate officials and in the end was driven into exile.
translations.idiomatic: yet in office he was repeatedly deceived by his subordinates and was finally banished.

sentences.zh: 所謂可與適道，未可與權。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by one who may be partnered on the Way but not entrusted with expedient power.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, he could walk the Way with you, but could not be trusted with power.

sentences.zh: 縱忠於國，能於官，孝於家，三者備矣，孰能繼之？

translations.literal: Zong was loyal to the state, capable in office, and filial at home — when all three were complete, who could follow him?
translations.idiomatic: Zong was loyal to the state, capable in office, and filial at home. When all three virtues were united in one man, who could match him?

sentences.zh: 鴻漸有衛社之功，非幹城之責，時以任崔旰為非，則不然矣。

translations.literal: Hongjian had the merit of defending the altars of state but not the duty of shielding the walls; contemporaries took his appointment of Cui Han as wrong — this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian had merit in defending the dynasty but was not a fortress against rebellion. Some criticized his accommodation of Cui Han, but that judgment is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 且旰南拒貞節，北敗獻誠，宜以懷來，未可力制，終致歸國，豈非臧謀？

translations.literal: Moreover Han resisted Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north; he should have been won by kindness and could not be subdued by force; in the end he caused the region to return to the state — was this not a sound plan?
translations.idiomatic: Han had held off Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north. He had to be won by conciliation, not crushed by force. In the end he brought the region back to the empire. Was that not wise policy?

sentences.zh: 向討之，即為劇賊矣。

translations.literal: Had they attacked him instead, he would have become a fierce bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Had the court attacked him instead, he would have become a far more dangerous rebel.

sentences.zh: 然事佛僥福，朋勢取容，非君子之道焉。

translations.literal: Yet in serving Buddhism to seek fortune and currying favor through factional power he did not follow the way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in seeking fortune through Buddhism and currying favor through factions he fell short of the way of a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：玄宗失德，祿山肆逆。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Xuanzong lost virtue and Lushan wildly rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Xuanzong lost his virtue, and An Lushan rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 見素竭節，諸公協力。

translations.literal: Jiansu exhausted his integrity and the various lords joined their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jiansu gave his utmost, and these men worked together in the state's service.
